issues.decision: Replace the generic 5.3L ring-wear claim and universal parts list with bulletin 10-06-01-008M's exact AFM engine RPOs, measurement threshold, diagnostic branches and production-date-dependent repairs.

evidence.label: GM Service Bulletin 10-06-01-008M - AFM Engine Oil Consumption

engines: AFM V8 with RPO LH9, L94, LZ1, L99, LC9, LH6, L76, L92, LFA, LMG or LY5
after.title: AFM Oil Spray or PCV Carryover Can Increase Oil Consumption (10-06-01-008M)
after.description: GM bulletin 10-06-01-008M applies to 2007-2014 Tahoe vehicles with the listed Active Fuel Management V8 engine RPOs. On higher-mileage vehicles, oil pulled through the PCV system or discharged from the AFM pressure-relief valve during certain drive cycles can contribute to piston-ring deposits, oil consumption, rough running, an illuminated service-engine lamp, and cracked or fouled spark plugs 1 or 7. The bulletin defines excessive consumption for this procedure as more than one quart per 2,000-3,000 miles after confirming the PCV system operates correctly.
after.solution: Verify the engine RPO, build date, PCV operation and measured oil-use rate before applying the bulletin. The GM procedure branches by cause and production date: it may call for the updated valve cover, an AFM oil deflector, cylinder decarbonizing, spark-plug replacement, or further piston/ring work after the bulletin tests. Do not assume every 5.3L Tahoe needs pistons or an AFM delete.
symptoms: Measured oil use greater than one quart per 2,000-3,000 miles
Rough running or service-engine lamp on a bulletin-listed AFM engine
Cracked or oil-fouled spark plug 1 or 7
Condition confirmed after checking PCV operation

citations.title: GM Service Bulletin 10-06-01-008M - AFM Engine Oil Consumption

issues.decision: Retain the safety issue using recall 25V-274 and add the current NHTSA remedy and scope investigations while keeping recall eligibility VIN-specific.

evidence.label: NHTSA Recall 25V-274 - L87 Connecting-Rod and Crankshaft Manufacturing Defects
NHTSA Recall Query RQ26-001 - Post-Remedy L87 Engine Failures
NHTSA Engineering Analysis EA25-007 - L87 Failures Outside Recall Scope

after.title: L87 Connecting-Rod or Crankshaft Defect Can Cause Engine Failure (25V-274)
after.description: NHTSA recall 25V-274 includes certain 2021-2024 Tahoe vehicles with the 6.2L L87 V8 built within the suspect manufacturing window. GM identified rod-bearing damage associated with sediment in connecting rods or crankshaft oil galleries and out-of-specification crankshaft dimensions or surface finish. Engine damage can cause loss of propulsion and increase crash risk. NHTSA subsequently opened RQ26-001 to evaluate alleged failures after the recall remedy and EA25-007 to evaluate reported L87 failures outside the original recall scope; those investigations do not themselves expand the recall population.
after.solution: Check the VIN for open recall 25V-274 and follow the dealer campaign. Dealers inspect the engine and repair or replace it as necessary; vehicles that pass inspection receive the specified higher-viscosity oil, a new oil-fill cap, a replacement oil filter and an owner-manual insert. Because the remedy and scope are under active NHTSA review, report a post-remedy failure or an apparently out-of-scope loss of propulsion to NHTSA and GM rather than assuming the recall procedure guarantees that every possible failure has been resolved.
symptoms: Knocking, banging or unusual engine noise
Check-engine warning before or during failure
Reduced propulsion or loss of propulsion
VIN included in recall 25V-274

after.title: Condenser Coupler Can Crack and Leak Refrigerant (Special Coverage 17336)
after.description: GM Special Coverage 17336 identifies certain 2015-2017 Tahoe vehicles whose air-conditioning condenser may crack at the specific coupler joining the combined transmission-fluid/oil cooler and condenser section. Thermal cycling can create the crack and allow refrigerant to escape, reducing or eliminating A/C cooling. The coverage was VIN-specific and does not support a blanket 2015-2020 condenser-failure claim.
after.solution: Confirm the leak location with proper refrigerant-system diagnosis and check the VIN and current GM campaign history. For the exact condition, the bulletin directs condenser replacement. The original special-coverage term was five years or 60,000 miles from first service and is likely expired for these vehicles, so do not promise a free repair without current VIN confirmation.

VIN listed in Special Coverage 17336

issues.decision: Replace the electronic-throttle-system failure assumption with PIP4578B's exact V8 carbon-buildup diagnosis, cleaning and idle-relearn procedure.

evidence.label: GM Preliminary Information PIP4578B - Throttle-Body Carbon and Idle Learn

after.title: Throttle-Body Carbon Can Cause Idle Surge, Hesitation or Reduced Power (PIP4578B)
after.description: GM preliminary information PIP4578B applies to 2006-2018 V8 Tahoe vehicles. On a high-mileage vehicle, carbon buildup can cause the control module to learn an increased throttle-plate angle. Enough buildup can contribute to idle or deceleration surge, tip-in hesitation, reduced-engine-power mode and defined throttle/idle DTCs. This does not prove the throttle body, pedal or wiring has failed.
after.solution: Use normal GM diagnostics to confirm the condition. If carbon buildup matches PIP4578B, clean the throttle body and perform the required throttle/idle learn reset with a scan tool. The relearn is also important after relevant module programming. Do not replace the throttle body, pedal assembly or wiring solely because a reduced-power message appeared.
symptoms: Idle or deceleration surge on a high-mileage vehicle
Tip-in hesitation
Reduced Engine Power message with a bulletin-listed throttle or idle DTC
Substantial throttle-body carbon buildup confirmed during diagnosis

citations.title: GM Preliminary Information PIP4578B - Throttle-Body Carbon and Idle Learn

after.contentUpdateSummary: Replaced the eleven-year electronic-throttle failure assumption with PIP4578B's exact 2006-2018 V8 carbon mechanism, symptom set, cleaning and idle-relearn procedure.

after.title: Collapsed or Stuck AFM Lifter Can Cause a Misfire or Tick (15-06-01-002O)
after.description: GM bulletin 15-06-01-002O applies to 2015-2020 Tahoe vehicles with the listed 5.3L or 6.2L engines. A mechanically collapsed or stuck Active Fuel Management lifter, damaged internal locking pin, lifter stuck in its bore, or bent pushrod can produce a tick, misfire, illuminated MIL and stored P0300. The bulletin does not establish inevitable failure on every AFM/DFM engine from 2007 through 2020.
after.solution: Follow GM service-information diagnosis and verify valve operation. If the affected valve is not moving, inspect the camshaft and lifters and replace the valve-lifter oil manifold and affected bank of AFM lifters as indicated. Replace a damaged camshaft only when inspection confirms excessive lobe or roller wear; do not disable AFM or replace every lifter based only on a generic misfire code.
symptoms: Consistent engine tick from the valvetrain
Engine misfire with MIL illuminated
DTC P0300 after diagnosis isolates the valve concern
Confirmed collapsed or stuck AFM lifter or bent pushrod

evidence.label: GM Preliminary Information PIT5801E - Air-Ride Level, Sag and Service Messages

after.title: Partially Seated Air Line Can Cause Sag, Lean or Air-Suspension Messages (PIT5801E)
after.description: GM preliminary information PIT5801E applies to 2021-2025 Tahoe vehicles with F47 Air Ride Suspension. An air line that is not fully inserted at an air spring, controller or reservoir fitting can leak and underinflate a spring. At an air-spring fitting, the internal check valve can instead trap air and overinflate that spring, making the opposite side appear low. The condition can produce an uneven ride height, leveling-unavailable, service-air-suspension or speed-limited messages and listed chassis DTCs.
after.solution: Confirm F47 equipment and follow PIT5801E to inspect the marked insertion depth at every relevant fitting before replacing an air spring, compressor or controller. Fully seat or repair the affected line/fitting as directed, then verify ride height and system operation. This bulletin does not support the frozen 2007-2020 claim that compressor and air-spring replacement is universally required.
symptoms: Vehicle sits unevenly or leans
One corner sags or appears overinflated
Leveling Unavailable or Service Air Suspension message
Speed Limited message with a bulletin-listed chassis DTC

citations.title: GM Preliminary Information PIT5801E - Air-Ride Level, Sag and Service Messages

evidence.label: NHTSA Engineering Analysis EA11-001 Closing Report - GMT800 Brake Pipe Corrosion

trims: GMT800 Tahoe vehicles in NHTSA-defined salt states
after.title: Age- and Salt-Related Hydraulic Brake-Pipe Corrosion (NHTSA EA11-001)
after.description: NHTSA engineering analysis EA11-001 examined corrosion failures in model-year 1999-2003 GMT800 trucks and utilities in salt states, which intersects the 2000-2003 Tahoe. The agency found failures strongly correlated with vehicle age and region and described general corrosion across the pipe assembly rather than a unique routing or retention defect. A ruptured pipe can reduce braking effectiveness, but NHTSA closed the investigation without identifying a safety-related defect or ordering a recall.
after.solution: On an older salt-exposed vehicle, have the full hydraulic pipe assembly inspected for leaks, heavy scaling, flaking and metal loss. The report says GM recommends replacing the entire pipe set when any pipe leaks or is corroded severely enough to require replacement, using the correct pre-formed kit. This is not a recall or automatic free repair, and surface appearance should be evaluated by a qualified brake technician.
symptoms: Visible heavy scaling or flaking on hydraulic brake pipes
Brake-fluid leak from a corroded pipe
Red BRAKE warning after fluid loss or pressure imbalance
Reduced braking effectiveness after a hydraulic circuit fails

citations.title: NHTSA Engineering Analysis EA11-001 Closing Report - GMT800 Brake Pipe Corrosion
